items.title: The Peshmerga fought ISIS. They're now ready to go war for their homeland
items.description: On Iraq's border with Iran troops are amassing as Iranian Kurds from across the globe gather to revolt after 47 years of being the victims of an oppressive and cruel regime.

items.title: Trump's war tests his 'maybe less enthusiastic' VP Vance
items.description: From MAGA-loathing "hillbilly" to vice-president, JD Vance's rise and rebirth has been something to behold. But the war in Iran may test his considerable political dexterity.

items.title: Fuel quality rules relaxed to rush 100 million litres into Australia's supply
items.description: Australia will bring in 100 million more litres of petrol by allowing a higher level of sulfur content in its fuel for the next 60 days, Energy Minister Chris Bowen says, as the country reckons with petrol flows choked by the Middle East war.

items.title: Motorists urged to stop panicking and hoarding fuel as oil price surges
items.description: The oil price has surged again amid Iranian strikes on oil tankers and the fear there could be more attacks to come.

items.title: Oil tankers burn as Iran's new leader vows to keep Strait of Hormuz closed
items.description: Iran's new supreme leader says the Strait of Hormuz should remain closed as a tool of pressure, vowing to "obtain compensation from the enemy".

items.title: Britain and the US had a special bond. This war might have changed that
items.description: Many nations, including Australia, claim to have a special relationship with the United States. Britain, and some in Europe, are finding out that's no longer the case.

items.title: The full-throttle North Korean side looking to rain on the Matildas' parade
items.description: Sensational protests, head-scratching substitutions and some seriously impressive play — North Korea is one of Asian Cup's best sides, and certainly its most mysterious. Here is what the Matildas can expect in their blockbuster quarterfinal tonight in Perth.

items.title: Blues hang on for scratchy but vital win over Tigers at the MCG
items.description: Carlton kicks only one goal in the second half, but it is just enough to hold off a late charge by a wayward Richmond at the MCG.

items.title: 'Absolute madness': Broncos remain winless after Eels win bizarre NRL clash
items.description: The Broncos' defence is labelled "pathetic" as they surrender a 20-6 lead, hit back in the second half but eventually lose 40-32 on the back of future teammate Jonah Pezet's game-sealing try.

items.title: Phones seized, families threatened: The bid to save Iran's female footballers
items.description: Iranian activists are racing against time to convince members of the country's female football team to turn back from Malaysia, as fears grow that the women are being coerced home by regime officials.

items.title: This MP's electorate gets the largest the CGT discount. She wants to rein it in
items.description: New analysis shows five of the six electorates with the largest capital gains tax discount benefits are held by independents.

items.title: Iranian women's team highlights complex history of athletes seeking asylum abroad
items.description: The choice for some Iranian women's soccer team members to stay in Australia is not the first time athletes have travelled for a sporting competition and chosen to stay.

items.title: IDF drops prosecution of reservists who allegedly raped Palestinian detainee
items.description: Israel's military drops the prosecution of five reservists accused of the violent rape of a Palestinian man at the Sde Teiman prison, under the cover of the war with Iran.

items.title: Albanese government avoids the 'w' word
items.description: This week in Canberra the Nationals chose a new leader, the energy minister chose his words carefully and the government chose to avoid one word altogether.

items.title: How Pokémon taught Aussie insect fans how to catch 'em all
items.description: As Pokémon turns 30, a video game inspired by insect-collecting continues to shape how scientists think and teach about bugs today.

items.title: Why Hugo Weaving doesn't learn his lines before rehearsal
items.description: Hugo Weaving may be an internationally renowned actor of both stage and screen, but he says he never feels ready for his next big role.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: A new Nationals leader and a curious crocodile
items.description: Think you've been paying attention to the news cycle this week? Test your memory here.

items.title: Cruise ship had 'small margin for error' in poor light, report says
items.description: An early safety report into the grounding of luxury Australian cruise ship Coral Adventurer focuses on its speed and a wide turn in confined waters just before it swerved into a reef.

items.title: Grace Tame says her speaking events have stopped over 'smear campaign'
items.description: Former Australian of the Year Grace Tame says a conference in Hobart will be her last speaking engagement for the year, at this stage.

items.title: What should you do with the family home after a divorce?
items.description: For many Australians, the decision to divorce has become even more complicated because of the rising cost of housing. Some are now calling for policy changes to make it easier for single parents to re-enter the housing market.

items.title: Co-founder of Copenhagen's Noma steps down after abuse allegations
items.description: René Redzepi, co-founder of a restaurant repeatedly named the world's best, has announced he is stepping down after reports was abusive to staff at the famed Copenhagen restaurant.

items.title: Parents shocked by sudden closure of specialist service for kids with autism
items.description: In a statement published on Wednesday, early intervention care provider AEIOU announced the board had appointed external administrators to the organisation.

items.title: We asked, you told: Dog ownership dos and don'ts
items.description: Here's how you can become a more responsible dog owner — according to your fellow readers.

items.title: Another search, more frustration in Gus Lamont case
items.description: South Australian police have concluded their latest search for evidence following the disappearance of four-year-old Gus Lamont, but have not ruled out returning to the remote station where he lived.

items.title: The rise of the 'manosphere' is being felt in the classroom
items.description: Teachers say misogynistic behaviour from young, male students has been getting worse. Now there's a guide to help.
